intelligence.human_view: A 2-hour-20-minute read is not a listening experience — it is a book with a play button on it, and nobody finishes a book by accident. The decision here is not "add audio" — it is "distill first, then audio": the essence, ~1,500 words, ~10 minutes, in her voice, is what a person can actually hear in one sitting, and what his podcast people can turn around in 5–10 minutes. And the controls are part of the decision, not an afterthought — play without stop is a trap, and a trap is annoying, and annoying is the opposite of what the agreement is for. The full text stays on the page for reading and clicking through; the audio is the essence, not a replacement.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a very long story — so long it would take all afternoon to read out loud! So we make a short, beautiful version — just the most important parts, about ten minutes — that you can listen to like a podcast. And the play button always has a stop button and a pause button too, so you are always in charge.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the whole agreement is very long to listen to, dear — over two hours, dear! So we make a lovely short version, dear, about ten minutes, dear, just the most important parts in her voice, dear — and the play button always has a stop and a pause, dear, so you are always in charge, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: DISTILL IT SO IT'S AUDIO-PERFECT. A PODCAST-STYLE READ. PLAY MUST HAVE STOP, PAUSE, PLAY. THE FULL TEXT STAYS; THE AUDIO IS THE ESSENCE.
